cards.body: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no plans for Huang to return. Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the company’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.) Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity. Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China. What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down. A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027. Tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country. Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China. And again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line. key_facts: 트럼프는 내각·보좌진과 사전 협의 없이 해외 데이터센터 건설 금지 또는 '막대한 세금' 부과를 언급했다 (Axios 보도)
**중국 AI 랩들이 법적 루프홀을 이용해 Nvidia의 수출 금지 칩(Blackwell, 예정된 Vera Rubin)을 탑재한 해외 데이터센터에 데이터를 보내고 있다**는 것이 금지 검토의 한 배경
미 하원은 이 루프홀을 막기 위한 Remote Access Security Act(RASA)를 2026년 1월 통과시켰으나 상원에서 계류 중
BIS(미 산업안보국)는 Nvidia에 고객사의 51% 이상이 비(非)중국 자본이어야 한다고 경고
미국 내 데이터센터 모라토리엄(건설 중단 조치)이 500건을 넘어섰고, 중간선거에서 관련 데이터센터 지원 법안들이 대부분 부결됨
summary_data.why_matters: 이 조치가 실제 입법화되면 **미국 기업이 데이터 주권(data sovereignty)을 요구하는 해외 시장을 상실**할 위험이 있으며, 동시에 Nvidia 칩의 중국 우회 수출 경로를 차단하려는 수출통제 강화 흐름과 직결된다. 다만 과세권은 의회에 있고 여당이 상·하원을 장악하지 못해 실행 가능성은 불확실하다.
summary_data.subject_angle: **Nvidia는 Blackwell·Vera Rubin 칩이 중국 우회 수출의 핵심 대상으로 지목**되면서 고객사 지분 구조(51% 비중국) 검증 등 컴플라이언스 부담이 커지고 있으며, 미국의 해외 데이터센터 규제 강화는 Nvidia 하이퍼스케일 고객들의 해외 투자 전략에도 영향을 줄 수 있다.

cards.body: President Donald Trump, who has been pushing for AI development in the U.S., said that he wants to prevent U.S. companies from building data centers in other countries or charge them with a “tremendous tax” if they push ahead with their overseas plans. The move comes as a surprise, Trump said, as he hasn’t even discussed the proposed policy with his cabinet and advisors, reports Axios . Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible “They’re making so much money they don’t know what to do with it,” the U.S. president said. He added that Americans should negotiate with AI hyperscalers that want to establish data centers in communities, as they could help reduce costs and taxes. “They have plenty of money. Take it,” Trump added. Several states and jurisdictions have started implementing similar solutions, with one Pennsylvania town listing 43 specific demands to approve an AI data center, while New York State recommended the municipalities demand a $1 million community investment per megawatt. Some developers embraced this, with one offering $10,000 per household if its 1,3000-acre facility gets approved, while Elon Musk’s SpaceX is buying out 418 homes near its flagship AI data center. This is going to be an issue for many Americans, though, especially as AI data center measures put forward in the recently concluded mid-term elections have been comprehensively defeated . In fact, data center moratoriums have already surged past 500 across the U.S., making it harder for developers to push forward with their projects. One possible reason Trump is considering a ban on overseas data centers for U.S. companies is that Chinese AI labs have been exploiting a loophole in U.S. law. This technicality has allowed them to export data to overseas data centers that use AI chips banned for export to China, like Nvidia’s Blackwell and upcoming Vera Rubin chips. “We’re not allowing data centers to go into other countries because China will take all of them, and we’re not allowing that to happen,” Trump said. The U.S. House of Representatives passed the Remote Access Security Act (RASA) in January 2026 to close the workaround, but the bill has been in limbo in the Senate since then. The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is also taking steps to prevent this , with Nvidia warning its clients that their customers should be at least 51% not from China to avoid legal exposure. NVIDIA CPU 책임자 Ian Finder는 NVIDIA가 에이전틱 AI 모멘트를 예측했다는 것은 'absurd'라며, 대신 '제품 직관(product intuition)'이 Vera 설계를 이끌었다고 언급
AMD는 자사 Instinct MI430X의 네이티브 FP64 연산이 NVIDIA의 Ozaki FP64 에뮬레이션 방식보다 메모리 사용 측면에서 우월하다고 주장
AMD는 TOP500 신규 시스템의 40% 이상을 차지(전년 대비 14%p 상승)하며 Lux(14위), Discovery(2028년 데뷔 예정) 시스템 보유
summary_data.why_matters: NVIDIA는 Rubin HPC와 Vera CPU를 통해 **AI 가속과 전통 HPC 컴퓨팅의 경계를 허무는 통합 컴퓨팅 스택 전략**을 추진 중이며, 이는 TOP500 등 전통 슈퍼컴퓨팅 벤치마크에서 AMD의 약진에 대응하는 움직임으로 해석된다. 동시에 AMD는 FP64 네이티브 지원과 이종 컴퓨트 스택 전략으로 NVIDIA의 에뮬레이션 기반 정밀도 접근을 직접 공격하고 있어 HPC·AI 융합 시장에서 경쟁이 심화되고 있다.

cards.body: In case you're worried about missing out on all the goodness on Tom's Hardware Premium , we've rounded up everything that we've published this week right here. The main theme for this week has been coverage straight from the show floor at the annual Supercomputing conference ( SC26 ). If you've not yet caught up, you've been missing out, as all of our coverage from the conference is currently free to access. All you need to do is sign up or log in to your Tom's Hardware account to enjoy all of our coverage from the show. First up, our resident CPU boffin, Jake Roach, has been on the show floor all week, offering us a direct line to all the goings-on at the conference, including an interesting back-and-forth from Nvidia and AMD on their CPUs. AMD claims that its latest EPYC Venice lineup is the best at agentic workloads, while Nvidia's marketing material characterized Nvidia's Vera CPU as being purpose-built for Agentic AI. At SC26, Nvidia CPU chief Ian Finder rebuked Nvidia's own marketing material, stating that the idea that Nvidia could have predicted the Data Center moment was "absurd," instead saying that the company's design know-how helped them develop the processor. In this interview, we sit down with Finder to find out how Vera came to be, what agentic workloads mean for the CPU industry, and where Nvidia's headed next. Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume it predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development – ‘product intuition’ helped drive CPU design, superior memory bandwidth will play critical role in future AI agents, CPU boss claims Nvidia's Vera CPU was a hot topic at SC26, as the company explained that existing software cannot always take full advantage of the processor without architecture-specific optimization. The company showed that under some workloads, Vera's performance can be optimized by up to 39% when taking its Olympus-based Arm cores into account. However, it remains to be seen how much performance can be gained from Olympus-specific hardware optimization workloads other than matrix multiplication. Nvidia claims its Vera CPU can gain up to 39% performance boost via software optimization at SC26 — architectural fine-tuning is needed to fully unleash custom Olympus cores (Image credit: Nvidia) Nvidia also announced a Rubin GPU variant, named Rubin HPC, a chip that the company claims is purpose-built for agentic workflows and scientific simulations that demand processing large datasets. While technical details remain scant, Nvidia says that Rubin HPC sports over 50,000 CUDA cores, or slightly below double the number of cores present in the standard-issue Rubin GPU. We explored all the details and possibilities that the newly announced chip might offer. Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026 — new chip accelerates agentic HPC workloads, arrives in 2028 AMD is now featured in over 40% of the new TOP500 list of supercomputers, with a 14% boost to the company's position.

headlines.title: One gigabyte of Wikipedia losslessly compressed to 105.39MB with self-learning AI transformer model

stage1.korean_title: 1GB 위키피디아를 105MB로 무손실 압축한 신경망 연구
stage1.korean_summary: Tufa Labs가 자기학습 트랜스포머로 Wikipedia 데이터를 압축했으며 NVIDIA B200 GPU를 활용했다.

headlines.body: Tufa Labs’ tufazip has compressed 1GB of information from Wikipedia into just 105MB of space, losslessly, without using any hand-built models, according to a research post . The method uses a 163-million-parameter Transformer model as a predictor instead, and similar compression or decompression would take two Nvidia B200 GPUs about a week to manage. It’s the smallest result on the Large Text Compression Benchmark from any entry that uses a neural network as its only predictor. We shrank 1 GB of Wikipedia to 105.39 MB, losslessly. Introducing tufazip: the best entry on the Large Text Compression Benchmark using a neural network as its sole predictor. Everything above it mixes a transformer with hand-built models. November 19, 2026 Researcher Tommy He built tufazip, and the full package, at 105.39MB after optimization, includes a small, 4.33MB pre-trained starter model — stored at low precision, or quantized, to save space — that’s needed to unpack the file. The full model is a 12-layer Transformer, which means there are 12 stages for each guess to go through. The starter stores just two already-trained stages, copying them back and forth to fill all 12 once the full model spins up in memory; each copy keeps learning on its own. (Image credit: Tufa Labs ) This doesn’t work like a traditional chatbot or cloud AI but is, rather, a self-contained language model that learns on the fly. Notable here is that this compression is lossless, which means there’s no risk of any data being lost in the process. This means that predictor updates must be “fully deterministic.” Training happens in two stages. The starter, a 34-million-parameter model, is trained offline, before any compression begins. Then, the full model begins to learn online, by predicting each token and training on it, with the unpacking side repeating the same steps, with the model itself being rebuilt alongside the text. For this reason, the total size must include, besides the compressed text, only the unpacking program and the files it needs, including the starter, but not the full trained model. There is no traditional, hand-built compression model that assists, setting it apart, Tufa Labs says, from all 12 entries that now rank above it on the benchmark, which mix a Transformer with hand-built models. Its first, online-only version ranked second when submitted in early September; the 105.39MB version was 13th as of the benchmark’s Nov. 19 update. Emphasis should be placed on this being a text-only benchmark, for those imagining media files. While this sounds more exciting than, say, WinRAR, it’s for research purposes and not a product, and that’s underlined by what you’d need to actually run it. Currently, two Nvidia B200 GPUs — plus two Intel Xeon Platinum 8570 CPUs in the test machine — would need 631,548 seconds to compress and 645,748 seconds to decompress the 105.39MB version, or about 7.3 and 7.5 days, respectively, not counting the starter’s offline training. headlines.body: 이번 주 국내 증시는 인공지능(AI) 산업의 성장 기대와 미국 통화정책 불확실성 사이에서 방향성을 탐색할 것으로 보인다. 22일 한국거래소에 따르면 지난 20일 코스피는 전 거래일 대비 267.93(5.21%) 하락한 4869.96에 장을 마감했다. 지난주 국내 증시는 엔비디아 호실적에도 AI 투자 지속성에 대한 우려와 미국 금리 인상 경계감이 겹치면서 큰 폭으로 하락했다. 주 초반 반등을 시도했지만 외국인 매도와 미국 기술주 약세가 이어지면서 코스피는 9개월 만에 5000선을 내줬다. 주중 등락을 거듭하던 코스피는 마지막 거래일인 20일 5% 넘게 떨어지며 투자심리가 크게 위축됐다. 전문가들은 AI 산업의 성장 기대가 여전히 유효하지만, 당분간 미국 금리와 외국인 수급에 따라 변동성이 이어질 수 있다고 진단했다. 이번 주 증시에 영향을 미칠 주요 변수로 미국 10월 개인소비지출(PCE) 물가와 미국 연방준비제도(Fed·연준)의 통화정책 방향, 외국인 수급 등을 꼽았다. 이번 주 코스피 예상 밴드는 5000~6100선이 제시됐다. 이경민 대신증권 연구원은 “엔비디아가 시장 예상치를 웃도는 실적과 매출 가이던스를 제시하면서 AI 산업의 견조한 수요가 재확인됐다”면서도 “미국의 대중 AI 반도체 수출 규제와 경영 불확실성, 연준의 매파적 기조는 여전히 우리 증시에 부담으로 작용한다”고 말했다. 특히 미·중 정상회담 이후 무역 갈등의 향방과 미국 연말 소비가 이번 주 시장의 관심사다. 지난 19일 열린 미·중 정상회담에서 양국은 무역휴전 연장에 원칙적으로 합의했지만 AI 반도체 규제와 희토류 수출 통제 등 핵심 쟁점에서는 입장 차를 좁히지 못했다. 관련 논의가 12월 주요 20개국(G20) 정상회의로 미뤄진 만큼 후속 협상 과정에 시선이 쏠린다. 오는 27일 시작되는 미국 블랙프라이데이도 연말 소비 기대를 자극할 변수다. 이 연구원은 “코스피 5000선 전후는 기업의 기초체력이 훼손됐다기보다 투자심리 위축과 외국인 매도세가 반영돼 주가가 실제 가치보다 낮아진 구간”이라며 “주가가 기업 가치에 맞게 회복될 것으로 보고 주식 비중을 확대하는 의견을 유지한다”고 설명했다. 미국 금리 경로와 외국인 매도세도 국내 증시의 반등을 제한할 변수로 꼽힌다. 강진혁 신한투자증권 연구원은 “실적 시즌이 종료되면서 다시 거시경제 변수와 시장을 움직이는 주요 재료에 따라 증시 흐름이 달라질 수 있다”며 “미국 PCE 물가를 통해 연준의 금리 경로를 확인할 필요가 있다”고 밝혔다. 유은정 기자 viayou@chosunbiz.com

headlines.title: Homelabber’s second-gen Optane build uses two RTX 3090s to run 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi AI model at 3.11 tokens per second

stage1.korean_title: 2세대 Optane 빌드: RTX 3090 2개로 2.8조 파라미터 AI 모델 운영
stage1.korean_summary: PC 애호가가 RTX 3090 2개를 활용해 Moonshot Kimi 대규모 AI 모델을 개인 환경에서 실행했다.

headlines.body: A homelabber detailed improvements to the second-gen Optane AI build in a follow-up post on Reddit , showing the addition of two RTX 3090s to run the 2.8-trillion-parameter Moonshot Kimi K3 model at 3.11 tokens per second. Transferring almost half the model onto a RAM drive added a significant 41% to generation speed and 26% to prompt evaluation. The extra fans are still needed, though, as the persistent Optane memory gets very hot. Follow-up: Kimi K3 Q2_K on second-gen Optane + 2× RTX 3090 — 3.11 t/s generation, 16.8 t/s prompt eval from r/homelab That speed is not the most impressive, but it comes with 16.8 tokens per second for prompt evaluation, with 45 of 94 shards, or 414 GB out of 865 GB, living on a RAM drive. Such an arrangement is not new to enthusiasts who would set aside system memory for extra-fast performance in a pseudo-non-volatile manner — it’s still volatile, but appears like a disk — although not everyone has that much RAM sitting around free these days. With both GPUs but no RAM drive, the build ran at 2.20 tokens per second for generation and 13.3 for prompt evaluation. Kimi K3 Q2_K with two RTX 3090s: model in Optane vs. partly in a RAM drive Configuration Where the model is stored Generation (tokens/s) Prompt evaluation (tokens/s) Optane only All 94 shards in Optane 2.20 13.3 RAM drive + Optane 45 of 94 shards (414 GB of 865 GB) in a tmpfs RAM drive, the rest in Optane 3.11 16.8 Change — About 41% faster About 26% faster Builder’s measurements; llama.cpp, DAX on for the Optane portion. Even a quick read of the details makes it clear that the GPUs aren’t holding the model: two RTX 3090s, at 24 GB apiece, only have a total of 48 GB of VRAM, which is about 5.5% of the 865 GB model file. That said, the model is a mixture-of-experts (MoE) type, where its weights are split into multiple “experts” with only a few run per token. Any given token will have “routed” experts selected for it, while “shared” experts run on every token. For this model, with 896 experts, 16 are chosen per token, with two shared, with an active 104B parameters out of its 2.8T. All 2.8T parameters would take about 5.6 TB at 16-bit precision. Moonshot’s own release, which uses the 4-bit MXFP4 format, comes to about 1.56 TB, and the Q2_K file used here shrinks that to 865 GB, an average of under 3 bits per parameter. The 865 GB figure is likely in gibibytes (GiB), but for clarity we’re using the GB values as written by the homelabber. The configuration here has the routed-expert tensors stay on the CPU side, originally in Optane, and now in Optane plus the RAM drive. The RTX 3090s handle attention, or how each token weighs the rest of the context, and the dense feed-forward network layer that isn’t split into experts, where every token passes through it. They also manage the shared experts, other active-dense components, the KV cache, and the stored context of the current conversation, with the GPU compute buffers. headlines.body: 인공지능(AI) 인프라 투자 확대로 메모리와 반도체 수급 부담이 커지면서 PC 시장, 특히 게이밍 디바이스 시장도 영향을 받고 있다. 그래픽처리장치(GPU)와 메모리, 그래픽카드 가격이 상승하는 가운데 엔비디아는 수익성이 높은 데이터센터용 GPU에 사업 역량을 집중하고 있다. AMD와 인텔도 데이터센터용 칩을 전략적 우선순위에 두고 있다.하지만 발상을 바꾸면 의외로 게임을 즐길 현실적인 대안은 가까운 곳에 있다. 4K 해상도에 최고 그래픽 풀옵션을 고집하지 않는다면 일상에서 흔히 접하는 노트북 PC로도 충분히 게임을 즐길 수 있다.
